Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear ask.

I've assembled a concise audit pack and included an initial action list for gaps we typically see in bank reviews. Attached: 'nexabank-architecture-diagram-v2.pdf' and 'controlplane-dataflow-matrix.xlsx' plus a short runbook snippet pasted below. Also linking to our SOC2 letter in Drive.

Quick notes up-front:
- The attached PDF highlights the control plane (control-plane API endpoints, auth, KMS/HSM integration) vs the data plane (inference workers, tenant network namespaces, egress proxies). Demarc is at the ingress edge + egress proxy; we recommend a small egress filtering appliance on the customer side for additional outbound controls.
- Egress controls: we use enforced egress lists per-tenant plus optional TLS interception via a customer-provided proxy (documented). Certificate rotation for service certs is driven by our control plane and mirrored to runtime nodes; hardware KMS/HSM integration is supported (see diag legend).

Runbook excerpt (paste):
1) Tenant isolation: new tenant slot creation creates strict RBAC + network namespace; default deny ingress between tenant namespaces.
2) Failover: control-plane elects new leader, KV state restored from encrypted snapshot; data-plane workers drain and reconnect on new control-plane endpoint.
3) Egress incident: flip to sinkhole route + notify ops, collect K/V cache snapshot, rotate ephemeral creds.

Action items we propose:
- We can produce a redacted topology with your IP ranges and crossconnect labels if you want stronger evidence for the GRC team. (Needs a short SOW)
- Provide an ops-runbook excerpt as plain text for chain-of-custody proof.

I'll loop Karthik and Marissa for any low-level diagrams and to confirm cert/KMS wording. If that works, we'll send a consolidated PDF and the matrix by EOD tomorrow.

— Soojin
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
(attachment: nexabank-architecture-diagram-v2.pdf, controlplane-dataflow-matrix.xlsx)

Oliver / Soojin — adding a few technical clarifications and the list of supporting artifacts we'll include in the final bundle.

Clarifications:
- Control plane: runs in the customer VPC if you're on Private (VPC) mode; the control-plane control plane endpoint is reachable only over the management peering; all control plane traffic is mutually authenticated with mTLS and bound to our service identity.
- Data plane: inference nodes are in customer subnet(s) with only egress to approved endpoints; we recommend an egress NAT + proxy for auditing. KV cache stays local to the node and is encrypted at rest.

Supporting artifacts to include:
- High-level diagram (PDF) — where demarc points are labeled and legend describes KMS, mTLS, egress proxy
- Control/data flow matrix (XLSX) — event examples, ports, protocol, auth method, SLOs for control messages
- Short ops-runbook excerpt (TXT) — tenant on/offboarding, failover steps, rotation steps
- Cert rotation summary (TXT) — cadence, automated rotation, key owner
- Redaction-friendly evidence template (DOCX) — so your GRC team can hide IPs and still keep topology context

I'll attach the runbook snippet and cert summary to the consolidated PDF. If NexaBank wants us to include a pre-redacted copy with your ASNs and subnet labels, we can do that under an SOW and a simple NDAs attachment.

— Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
